::: {#prp-panda-rise-dress}
Discussion to highlight how dynamical rules can be simple since they deal only with instantaneous motion. 

A non-dynamical-rule description of motion: Kepler's theory of planetary motion: Planets trace out elliptical orbits with the Sun at one focus and sweep out equal areas in equal times. This is a macroscopic description. 

A description in terms of a dynamical rule involves two relatively simple parts: (1) The planet's rate-of-change in position is velocity.  (2) The rate-of-change in velocity is directed toward the Sun and inversely proportional to the square of the distance from the Sun. 

The accounting system plays out this rule and, in consequence, produces orbits that are ellipses with the planet's velocity inversely proportional to distance from the Sun.

:::
